name: MMMU (Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning)
description: MMMU is a 11.5K-question Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning benchmark targeting college-level, expert-style perception and reasoning across 6 disciplines, 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 heterogeneous image types (e.g., charts, diagrams, medical scans, music sheets, chemical structures). Questions are interleaved text-image, mostly multiple-choice with some open-ended, curated from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources to evaluate LMMs on expert-level knowledge, perception, and reasoning.
citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.

creator.name: IN.AI Research; University of Waterloo; The Ohio State University; and collaborators (see author list)

rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollection: Collected manually by 50+ university students (including co-authors) across selected college subjects using textbooks, exams, quizzes, and online resources; annotators avoided sources prohibiting copying/redistribution and preferred problems without immediately available answers; data cleaning removed duplicates via lexical/source similarity, standardized formatting/typo fixes, and filtered out ~10% very easy items; difficulty labeled (easy/medium/hard), image types tagged, and explanations included for a subset.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom/user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification (internal), plus manual curation; JSON format specified for samples.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:annotatorDemographics: Approximately 50 university students from various majors (including co-authors); 3 human student experts per subject were used for human baseline evaluation.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal models on expert-level perception, knowledge, and reasoning; evaluating LMM performance across disciplines, image types, and difficulty; error analysis of perception/knowledge/reasoning; progress tracking toward Expert AGI; zero-shot and few-shot evaluation.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal/sensitive data intended; questions sourced from public/educational materials; ethical guidance emphasized avoiding private information and respecting copyright/licensing.
